tagline: Up one wild river, over the divide, and down another.
intro: Out of Roseburg, OR 138 runs east through oak-dotted hills to Glide and takes up the North Umpqua there. The river is held in high regard by anglers, and thirty miles of it are fly-fishing-only water, all reachable from the road. The byway passes fifteen waterfalls in all, Watson Falls among them at 272 feet, on the way up to Diamond Lake between Mount Bailey and Mount Thielsen.

At the south end of the lake it turns west and picks up the Rogue near Union Creek, where the old Fort Klamath military wagon road ended. Then it is downhill with the river to Prospect, Shady Cove and Gold Hill.
season: June through October, by the state's trip notes. Expect snow at the higher elevations.

moments.title: Glide
moments.text: At the Colliding Rivers the Little River runs straight into the North Umpqua, one of the few places anywhere where two rivers meet head-on.

moments.title: Toketee Falls
moments.text: The North Umpqua drops about 120 feet in two stages through old columnar basalt, at a falls whose name is Chinook Jargon for pretty or graceful.

moments.title: Mount Thielsen
moments.text: The spire over Diamond Lake is struck by lightning so often that rocks on its summit have melted into a rare mineraloid. It is known as the lightning rod of the Cascades.
